name: mycareersfuture-jobs-scraper
title: MyCareersFuture Jobs Scraper (Singapore)
description: Scrape job postings from MyCareersFuture.gov.sg, Singapore's government job portal. Returns title, company, salary range, employment type, skills, address, dates, views, applications and description. Pay per result.
readme:
# MyCareersFuture Jobs Scraper: Singapore Job Listings Get job postings from [MyCareersFuture](https://www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/), the Singapore government job portal, as clean dataset rows. Search by keyword or list the newest jobs. Each row has the title, company, salary range, employment type, skills, work address, posting and closing dates, view and application counts and the full job description. ## What you can do with it - Track the Singapore job market by keyword, salary band or employment type, on a schedule. - Build lead lists of companies and agencies that are hiring, with their UEN number, website and industry. - Compare salary ranges per skill, category or position level. - Feed a job board, alert service or labour market report with current Singapore postings. ## What you get One dataset row per job. A job found by several searches is returned once, and duplicates are removed before anything is charged, so the number of rows is the number of results you pay for. Missing values are `null`, lists are always lists (`[]` when empty). | Fields | Description | |---|---| | `id`, `job_post_id`, `title`, `job_url`, `posting_source`, `status` | Ids, title and the link to the job page | | `company_name`, `company_uen`, `company_logo`, `company_url`, `company_description`, `company_employee_count`, `company_ssic_code`, `company_ssic_description`, `company_responsive`, `posted_on_behalf` | The company that posted the job. For agency postings this is the agency | | `hiring_company_name`, `hiring_company_uen`, `hiring_company_logo`, `hiring_company_url`, `hiring_company_description`, `hiring_company_ssic_code`, `hiring_company_ssic_description` | The end employer, only when an agency posted the job for it | | `salary_min`, `salary_max`, `salary_currency`, `salary_period`, `salary_hidden` | Salary range as posted (Singapore dollars, usually per month) | | `experience_years_min`, `vacancies`, `categories`, `employment_types`, `position_levels`, `skills`, `flexible_work_arrangements`, `schemes` | Experience, categories, employment types, position levels, skills, flexible work and government schemes | | `ssoc_code`, `ssoc_version`, `occupation_id`, `ssec_eqa`, `ssec_fos` | Occupation and education codes (SSOC, SSEC) | | `address_block`, `address_street`, `address_building`, `address_postal_code`, `address_full`, `districts`, `regions`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `is_overseas` | Work address, postal districts and coordinates | | `posted_at`, `first_posted_at`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at` | Posting, first posting, closing, creation and update times (ISO 8601) | | `views`, `applications`, `repost_count`, `edit_count` | Public counters of the job page (need the detail record) | | `description`, `description_text`, `screening_questions` | Description as HTML and plain text, and screening questions (need the detail record) | | `details_fetched`, `relevance_score`, `search_rank`, `search_query` | `details_fetched` is true when the detail record was read. `relevance_score` and `search_rank` come from the site search. `search_query` is the keyword that found the job (null for the newest-jobs search) | | `source`, `scraped_at` | Site host, scrape time (UTC) | Salary is in Singapore dollars. With `includeDetails` off, or when a detail record fails, the detail-only fields are `null`. Dates without a time (`posted_at`, `first_posted_at`, `expires_at`) are ISO 8601 dates. ## Input | Field | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | `searchQueries` | string[] | Keywords, one search each. Leave the list empty (`[]`) to get the newest jobs across all categories. If the field is left out, the sample keyword `python` runs with 20 results | | `sortBy` | string | `relevance` (default, the site's own keyword ranking) or `newest` (most recently posted first). A run without keywords always lists the newest jobs | | `salaryMin` | integer | Only jobs with a monthly salary of at least this amount (default 0 = off) | | `employmentType` | string[] | Only jobs with one of these types, for example `Full Time`, `Part Time`, `Contract`, `Permanent`, `Temporary` (default empty = all) | | `includeDetails` | boolean | Read each job's detail record for the full description and the other detail fields (default `true`). `false` returns the search fields only, faster | | `maxResultsPerQuery` | integer | Cap per keyword, 1 to 1000 (default 50) | | `maxResults` | integer | Total cap across all keywords (default 0 = no limit) | The search, the order and the filters are the ones of the MyCareersFuture website, so a keyword returns the same jobs in the same order as the site. `salaryMin` and `employmentType` are applied by the site; the actor does not filter again, so a job the site returns with a salary slightly under your minimum is kept. The search results alone carry no description. With `includeDetails` on (default) the actor reads each job's detail record, with a few requests at a time, and a job whose detail record cannot be read is still returned with the search fields (`details_fetched` is `false`). The price per job is the same with or without details. Example input: ```json {"searchQueries": ["python"], "maxResults": 20} ``` ## Output example ```json { "id": "f387112c4729cc2e92deba284571e468", "job_post_id": "MCF-2026-1959183", "title": "Senior Python Software Engineer Platform Services - IMMEDIATE HIRING", "job_url": "https://www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/job/engineering/senior-python-software-engineer-platform-services-immediate-hiring-pathsource-consulting-f387112c4729cc2e92deba284571e468", "posting_source": "Employer Portal", "status": "Open", "company_name": "PATHSOURCE CONSULTING PTE. LTD.", "company_uen": "202300706G", "company_logo": "https://static.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/images/company/logos/31be0efc3dbd040a845b190dff1b6042/pathsource-consulting.png", "company_url": "https://www.path-source.com/", "company_description": "

", "description_text": "The client is a Singapore-based data consultancy seeking a hands-on Senior Data Platform Engineer to build and operate large-scale data ingestion and storage se...", "details_fetched": true, "relevance_score": 0.0312, "search_rank": 3, "search_query": "python", "source": "www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg", "scraped_at": "2026-11-06T09:00:00Z" } ``` ## Pricing Price: $0.001 start fee per run, then $0.0015 per job result ($1.50 per 1,000 jobs). The run is charged the platform start event once and one result event per job saved to the dataset. You can set a maximum cost for the run; the run stops with the status "Stopped at the max charge limit" and keeps everything delivered so far. ## FAQ **Does it need a login or an API key?** No. It reads the public job listings of MyCareersFuture. **How many jobs can one keyword return?** Up to 1000 per keyword with `maxResultsPerQuery`, as far as the site lists results for the search. Each result page holds 20 jobs and the run stops at the last page the site returns. **What does a run with an empty keyword list return?** The newest jobs across the whole site. Use `maxResults` to limit it. **Why did a run return 0 jobs?** Either nothing matches the keyword or your filters removed every row ("0 jobs found for ..."), or the site did not answer. In the second case the run ends as failed with a clear status message and only the start event is charged. **Are repeated jobs charged twice?** No. A job is saved and charged once per run, even if several keywords find it. A run that is restarted by the platform continues where it stopped and does not charge saved jobs again.
